subject: High 5xx/429 spike — gateway auth validation misclassifying JWT failures
messages:

Subject: Spike: large volume of 5xx/429 from Redwood since 08:45 PT

Hi Jonas —

Starting ~08:45 PST we began seeing a sharp increase in failures across our ingestion jobs to the Redwood API. Symptoms:
- ~20% request failure rate across the 08:45–09:05 window; client retries caused throughput collapse.
- Responses are a mix of 500/502 and bursts of 429.
- Our logs show repeated "invalid_token" and "auth_validation_error" strings, but the response codes on our side are 500/502 (not 401).

We've attached a short sample of request IDs and header dumps (hzn-logs-sample-20261201.txt). This is impacting our scheduled nightly backfills — can you triage immediately?

Request IDs example: r-0a1b2c3d, r-0a1b2c3e, r-0a1b2c40

We can be on a quick call now if helpful.

— Sam Patel
Ops Lead, Horizon Analytics

Sam, thanks — got the sample. We're scheduling a triage call at 09:40 PT. Planned immediate actions:
- Markus to surface auth/gateway logs and correlate request IDs.
- We'll temporarily route your traffic to an alternate auth-validator group that skips the new header-rewrite path (if safe) to see if failure rate improves.
- Please attach the full request/response pair if available; the partial dump suggests the gateway may be rewriting or dropping Authorization headers for some traffic.

Temporary mitigation suggestion (you can apply immediately): reduce client retry aggressiveness (3 retries, base backoff 500ms) and add jitter. This should reduce client-side retry amplification. We'll aim to have a root-cause hypothesis before 11:00 PT.

Attachments: none from our side yet.

— Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: markus.klein@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-01T10:18:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Spike: large volume of 5xx/429 from Redwood since 08:45 PT

TL;DR: auth-validation pool returned 502/500 for JWT validation failures due to a transient clock-skew + proxy header rewrite; gateway mapped these into 5xx/429 in the edge layer.

Details:
- Reproduced against request r-0a1b2c3d. The auth-validator service compared exp claim vs local time and returned an internal validation error when drift > 120s on a subset of pods.
- We also found the proxy layer (envoy rewrite filter deployed in canary last week) occasionally stripped the Authorization header on retried requests where connection pooling reused the upstream connection. When the header was absent the validator returned an internal error (service-level) that the edge erroneously aggregated and surfaced as 500/502 instead of 401.
- Rate-limiting behavior: client retries receiving 5xx were hitting the edge quota limiter and surfaced as 429 after a few retries — that explains the mixed 5xx/429 pattern.

Immediate mitigations applied (10:05 PT):
1) Scoped rollback of the envoy header-rewrite filter on the canary set.
2) Pinned Horizon traffic to the older auth-validator pool that has a looser time-sync guard.
3) Increased sync frequency of NTP on the affected infra nodes (restart scheduled).

I've attached the auth-service-stacktrace-20261201.log and gateway-headers-dump-20261201.txt with correlated request IDs. We're running a controlled test now to confirm error rate drops.

— Markus Klein
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai, Horizon Ops <ops@horizon-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T11:07:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Spike: large volume of 5xx/429 from Redwood since 08:45 PT — Exec summary

Evelyn — looping you in for visibility. Executive summary for leadership:
- Impact: Horizon Analytics observed ~20% elevated failure rate across ingestion between 08:45–09:15 PT. Client retries amplified load and caused quota/429 responses.
- Root cause hypothesis: an envoy header-rewrite canary combined with transient clock skew on a subset of auth-validator pods caused JWT validation failures to surface as internal 5xx/502 instead of 401. Edge quota enforcement then produced 429s on retry amplification.
- Mitigation applied: rollback of the header-rewrite canary for affected nodes; traffic pinned to stable auth validators; NTP sync escalated. Error rates improved in validation tests post-mitigation.

Customer asks: 1) a postmortem with timeline and corrective actions, 2) evaluation of account credit given business impact, and 3) confirmation of long-term fixes to prevent misclassification of auth errors.

I'll coordinate with Marissa and Markus on the postmortem and a proposed credit.

— Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: markus.klein@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Cc: Horizon Ops <ops@horizon-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Spike: large volume of 5xx/429 from Redwood since 08:45 PT — final update

Update (closing the on-call):
- Verified: after rollback and pinning, Horizon's test traffic error rate dropped from 18–22% down to <1% in a 30-minute validation window.
- Root cause: combination of (a) a canary envoy rewrite filter that stripped Authorization on some connection-reuse cases, and (b) two auth-validator pods with NTP drift >120s. The validator returned a service-level error when expiration checks failed; the edge layer misclassified that as 500 instead of 401.
- Remediation (short term): canary filter rolled back, auth-validator pool healthchecks tightened, NTP sync cron accelerated.
- Remediation (long term): add explicit mapping of auth-validation errors to 401/403 at the edge; add contract tests for header-preservation during envoys' connection reuse; add alerting on >30s clock drift on validators.

Next steps:
1) Marissa will send a customer-facing postmortem draft by EOD tomorrow.
2) Ops/Infra will schedule an incident retro with actionable owners (we'll create a JIRA SUP-4286).
3) Commercial (Jonas) to propose credit.

Attachments: gateway-headers-dump-20261201.txt, auth-service-stacktrace-20261201.log

— Markus Klein
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
